info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description:
Every state model: its entity, state field, initial state and record type. Automation
administrators only.

post.description:
A state model on an entity's choice field with its initial state, optionally for one record type
(fixed once created; a typed model is not recorded in changesets). Recorded in the open changeset
otherwise. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: This entity already has an active state model, or no open changeset to record into

get.description:
One state model: its entity, state field, initial state, whether it is active, its transitions and
`row_version`. Automation administrators only.

delete.description: Retires the model. Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: No open changeset to record into, or the row is owned by another layer

patch.description: Changes the fields given. Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: row_version mismatch, no open changeset to record into, or the model is owned by another layer

post.summary: Add a transition to a state model
post.description:
A named move from one state to another, with an optional privilege, guard expression, and entry
and exit actions. Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: This edge already exists, or no open changeset to record into

delete.description:
Records can no longer take it. Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only.
Audited.

409.description: No open changeset to record into, or the row is owned by another layer

patch.description: Changes the fields given. Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: row_version mismatch, the new (from_state, to_state) edge already exists, no open changeset to record into, or the transition is owned by another layer

post.summary: Move a record to another state
post.description:
Takes one transition of the record's state model, checking its conditions; a transition that
needs approval parks the record and submits the request instead. `If-Match` is optional. Needs
update rights on the record. Audited.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional expected row_version; absent means the record's current version

200.description: Success. For a transition that requires approval (M07 Phase F), the record is parked in the transition's pending state (`to_state`) and `approval_request_id`/`requested_state` are present

403.description: Caller lacks the required privilege, or the transition's own required_privilege

409.description: The record changed concurrently, or If-Match is not its current row_version

422.description: No transition is configured for this state change, its guard condition refused it, or a rule rejected the write

200.description: The approval is cancelled (or was already closed) and the record has left its pending state

403.description: Caller lacks {entity}.update, or is not the requester (an administrator may only release an already-closed approval)

409.description: The record is not waiting on an approval, or its approval was granted and is being carried out

get.description:
The transitions the record's state model allows from its current state, each with its name and
target state. Anyone who may read the record.

ApprovalPlan.description:
D-421 / M10 (Approval & Governance) — an ordered set of approval steps,
persisted on the request as `plan JSONB` (migration
`0185_approval_request_plan_step.sql`). This is a **pure extension** of
D-195's primitive, not a second one (guidelines §13): a plan-bearing
request is still one `approval_request` row running through
`submit`/`decide`/`sweep_expired`'s same lifecycle machinery — a plan just
tells `decide_step` how many steps there are and what each one requires,
instead of the flat `required_approvals` count every pre-D-421 caller
still uses unchanged.

`mode`/`approvers` (`any`/`all`/`n_of_m` over a list of opaque tokens) is
generic dual-control sequencing — this crate owns it because it never has
to interpret a token to run the math. **What it must never do** is turn a
token like `"role:finance_manager"` or `"position:manager_of_requester"`
into an actual user id — that resolution is XRM metadata knowledge
(roles, teams, org structure) this crate has none of (guidelines §1), so
it stays in `xrm_audit::approval::resolve_step_approvers` (ARCH-5's same
split: attome-approval runs the lifecycle, the engine layer resolves what
its own tokens mean). Every function below that needs "who may decide
this step" therefore takes an already-resolved `&[Uuid]`/`usize` from the
caller — it never touches `approvers` itself.

allOf.description:
Z10-T2: conditions, grouping, evidence and reminders. Flattened, so
the JSON keys sit on the step itself and a plan stored before them
reads with every default.

approvers.description:
Opaque tokens this crate never parses — e.g. `"user:<uuid>"`,
`"role:<uuid>"`. See the module-level doc comment above.

sla_minutes.description:
`None` means this step never times out on its own — it waits
indefinitely for a human decision (still subject to the request's
overall backstop `expires_at`/`sweep_expired`, see
`submit_with_plan`'s doc comment).

threshold.description:
Required only when `mode == NofM` — how many of this step's *named*
approvers (not counting any delegate standing in for one of them,
see `ApprovalStep::required_count`'s doc comment) must decide before
the step closes. Ignored for `Any`/`All`.

CancelTransitionBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transition/cancel` — withdraws the record's
open transition approval (requester only) and returns the record to the
state it came from; or, when that approval was already closed without
executing (rejected, expired, invalidated) but the record is still
parked, finishes returning it (the requester or an administrator).

comment.description: Recorded on the audit events. Optional.

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except the listed fields.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: an attribute of the entity holding the status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows; a state listed here needs one.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type (a `record_type` code of the entity) this model
governs; omit for the entity's model of every other record. Fixed once
created. A typed model is not recorded in changesets or bundles: make
it through this API in each deployment.

state_field.description: Must name an existing `Choice` attribute on `entity_logicalname`.

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): an approval plan (ordered `any`/`all`/`n_of_m`
steps of `user:`/`role:`/`team:`/`position:manager_of_requester`
tokens), validated with attome-approval's own validator. Requires
`pending_state`.

auto_condition.description:
M8-T3: an attome-rules condition over the record's fields (such as
`due_date < today()`). When it holds for a record in `from_state`,
the transition happens by itself, checked after each write and daily.

on_reject_state.description:
An option of the state field; defaults to `from_state`. Only allowed
with `approval_plan`.

pending_state.description:
An option of the model's state field, other than `from_state`,
`to_state` and the model's initial state. Required with, and only
allowed with, `approval_plan`.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

LockedState.description: M8-T2: a state in which a record is read-only except `editable`.

editable.description: The fields that may still change while the record is in `state`.

OnTimeout.description:
What happens when a step's `sla_minutes` elapses with nobody having
decided it yet — applied by `apply_step_timeout_with`, driven by the sweep
that reuses M51's notification-escalation poller
(`xrm_notification::poller`; see that crate's `approval_timeouts` module).

PaginatedResponse_AvailableTransition.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description:
One entry of `GET /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transitions` — drives UI buttons
and kanban drop targets. Never lists a transition the caller lacks
`required_privilege` for.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_StateModelListItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except listed fields.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this model — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change or retire it.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: the attribute holding the record's status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type this model governs; absent for the entity's
model of every record without one of its own.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except listed fields.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this model.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: the attribute holding the record's status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type this model governs; absent for the entity's
model of every record without one of its own.

StateReasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons a record may give for being in `state`.

StepExtras.description: Z10-T2: what a step may add to who decides it and how.

business_hours.description: SLA and reminder minutes count business hours only.

escalate_to.description: Who an escalation goes to (an approver token).

group.description: Consecutive steps with the same group run together, in parallel.

reminder_minutes.description: Remind the approvers this long after the step started waiting.

requires_human.description: A person decides, never an agent.

requires_step_up.description: The decider confirms with a fresh sign-in or second factor.

skip_unless.description: A rules expression; the step runs only when it is true.

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): when set, asking for this transition moves the
record to `pending_state` and opens a `attome-approval` request running
this plan; approval moves it to `to_state`. Omitted when absent.

auto_condition.description:
M8-T3: the condition that makes the transition happen by itself.
Omitted when absent.

guard_expression.description:
M45 attome-rules expression, evaluated on every write path with the
record's fields and `current_user`; fail closed.

on_reject_state.description: Where a rejection sends the record; absent means `from_state`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this transition (it may differ
from its model's: a project may add a transition to a platform model).

pending_state.description: The state the record sits in while the approval is open.

TransitionRequestBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transition` — a state change by target state.
Runs the generic record update path (identical to a `PATCH` of the state
field, M07 §4.1); `comment` is recorded on the audit event. No
`row_version` in the body: send `If-Match` for optimistic concurrency, or
omit it to transition from the record's current version.

approval_request_id.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): present only when the requested transition
requires approval. The record is parked in `to_state` (the pending
state) and this request decides it; approval moves the record to
`requested_state`. Omitted otherwise.

requested_state.description:
The state that was asked for, when an approval now stands between the
record and it. Omitted otherwise.

to_state.description:
The state the record is in now. For a transition that requires
approval (M07 Phase F) this is the transition's pending state, not the
one asked for — see `approval_request_id`.

UpdateStateModelBody.description:
Full replacement of the model's mutable fields (`entity_logicalname` is
the immutable identity, same posture as an entity's own `logicalname`).

locked_states.description: M8-T2: full replacement, like every field here.

UpdateTransitionBody.description:
Full replacement of the transition's mutable fields + optimistic
concurrency, same shape as `UpdateStateModelBody`. `from_state`/`to_state`
are optional: omitted keeps the edge's current end, present moves it —
validated exactly as on create (an option of the model's state field; a
second live edge with the same `(from, to)` is `409`).

oneOf.description:
Full replacement like every other field here: omitted clears the
approval (the transition happens on write again). See
`CreateTransitionBody::approval_plan`.

auto_condition.description:
Full replacement: omitted makes the transition a manual one again.
See `CreateTransitionBody::auto_condition`.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
